newsitem.title: CHINA: China to scale down Cheung Kong project.
newsitem.headline: China to scale down Cheung Kong project.

text.p: Approval for a long-delayed real estate project led by Hong Kong's Cheung Kong Holdings Ltd will soon be given, but it will be on a smaller scale than originally planned, a senior official said on Monday.
The Orient Plaza, to be built in central Beijing, will involve investment of $1.8 billion instead of the originally-planned $2.2 billion, Beijing Vice-Mayor Zhang Baifa told reporters at a reception.
The area of the office block and shopping centre, just off Tiananmen Square, will be reduced to about 580,000 square metres from 800,000-900,000 square metres, Zhang said.
It would consist of three buildings rather than a single huge structure.
Construction was expected to begin soon and would take about three years, Zhang said.

Foundation work was halted in November 1994 amid complaints from city planners that the 70-metre high building would overshadow the Great Hall of the People, Tiananmen Square and the mausoleum of Chairman Mao Zedong.
"The main reason why it was delayed was because when (former city Communist Party chief) Chen Xitong was in charge he was not very democratic and did not respect the opinions of experts," Zhang said.
"He (Chen) infuriated the experts and they blew the whistle," Zhang said. "Everything had to be done all over again."
However, he said no wrongdoing had been involved in allocation of permission for the project.
The redevelopment of the site forced McDonald's Corp to close its flagship store in China this month, among its most profitable.
